classification.difficultyReason: The supplied parts guide two calculator calculations, applying a percentage rise to each wage, explaining additive invariance through unchanged distances from the mean, and comparing the resulting spreads. These are routine linked procedures with no unsignposted insight.

content.prompt:
A small workshop has six employees. Their weekly wages are:
$\$250,\ \$400,\ \$450,\ \$550,\ \$600,\ \$750$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the population standard deviation for this set of data, rounded to the nearest dollar.

answer.worked:
Enter the six wages in the calculator's 1-variable statistics mode and select population standard deviation $\sigma_x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\sigma_x &\approx \$158.1139\\&\approx \$158\quad\text{(nearest dollar)}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Each employee receives a $\$30$ pay increase. Explain the effect that this increase will have on the standard deviation.

answer.short: Unchanged; the spread of the wages is unchanged.
answer.worked: Every wage and the mean increase by $\$30$, so each wage's distance from the mean stays the same. The standard deviation is unchanged.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Instead of the $\$30$ increase, every employee receives a 20% pay rise. Calculate the new population standard deviation to the nearest dollar.

answer.worked:
New wages: $\$300,\ \$480,\ \$540,\ \$660,\ \$720,\ \$900$. Enter these in 1-variable statistics mode and select $\sigma_x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\sigma_x &\approx \$189.7367\\&\approx \$190\quad\text{(nearest dollar)}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Which pay rise gives the smaller standard deviation: $\$30$ each or 20% each?

answer.worked: The $\$30$ pay rise leaves the standard deviation at approximately $\$158$. The 20% pay rise increases it to approximately $\$190$, so $\$30$ each gives the smaller standard deviation.
